extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate/graduate students learning algebraic topology (computing fundamental groups, covering spaces, and knot complements)
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques and rules for computing fundamental groups: using deformation retractions, van Kampen's theorem, presentations from attaching cells, Wirtinger presentations for knot complements, and the theory/classification of covering spaces with lifting properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deformation retraction preserves π1 (use to compute complements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a space X deformation retracts onto a subspace A, then π1(X) ≈ π1(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: R^3 − A (complement of a circle) deformation retracts onto S^1 ∨ S^2, so π1(R^3 − A) ≈ π1(S^1 ∨ S^2) ≈ Z. Methods to see such a deformation retraction include: (1) exhibiting an explicit retraction flow (push points toward the retract), (2) showing a small open neighborhood of the target deformation retracts onto it and that neighborhood is homeomorphic to the original space, then enlarging the neighborhood by homeomorphisms until it becomes the whole space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of linking on complements' fundamental groups
rubrics_metrics.description: The topology (linked vs unlinked) of components in R^3 affects the deformation retract and hence π1 of the complement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Complement of two unlinked circles A and B deformation retracts onto S^1 ∨ S^1 ∨ S^2 ∨ S^2, yielding π1 ≈ Z * Z. If A and B are linked, the complement deformation retracts onto S^2 ∨ (S^1 × S^1) so π1 ≈ π1(S^1 × S^1) ≈ Z × Z. Use geometric pictures to find an appropriate deformation retract (wedge sums, tori, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-point compactification does not change π1 in this setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Passing from R^3 − K to its one-point compactification S^3 − K can preserve π1 when the added region and its intersection with the complement are simply-connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice: write S^3 − K as union of R^3 − K and an open ball B (the compactification point plus complement of a large closed ball). If B and B ∩ (R^3 − K) are simply-connected (the latter homeomorphic to S^2 × R), van Kampen implies the inclusion R^3 − K ↪ S^3 − K induces an isomorphism on π1. This often simplifies computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute π1 of torus knots via mapping-cylinder decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: For the torus knot Km,n, construct a 2-dimensional complex X = Xm,n (quotient of S^1×I by identifications) that deformation retracts from S^3 − K; then apply van Kampen to Xm ∪ Xn to obtain a presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Xm and Xn are mapping cylinders of z ↦ z^m and z ↦ z^n respectively; Xm ∩ Xn is a circle. Each of Xm, Xn, and the intersection has π1 ≈ Z. A generator of π1(Xm ∩ Xn) maps in Xm to m times a generator and in Xn to n times a generator. Van Kampen yields π1(X) presented as ⟨a,b | a^m = b^n⟩ (denoted G_{m,n}). Notes: if m or n = 1, group is Z; center is generated by a^m = b^n; abelianization and torsion considerations determine m and n up to ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attaching 2-cells: presentation via relators from attaching loops (Proposition 1.26(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is obtained from a path-connected space X by attaching 2-cells e^2_α via maps ϕ_α : S^1 → X, then the inclusion X ↪ Y induces a surjection π1(X,x0) → π1(Y,x0) whose kernel is the normal subgroup N generated by the loops γ_α ϕ_α γ_α^{-1} (where γ_α are paths from the basepoint to the attaching basepoint). Thus π1(Y) ≈ π1(X)/N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose basepoint x0 and paths γ_α to each attaching point; the resulting conjugacy classes of attaching loops generate the normal subgroup to be quotiented out. The kernel does not depend on the choice of γ_α (only up to conjugacy). Use the construction of an auxiliary space Z and van Kampen on {A,B} as in the proof to justify the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attaching cells of dimension >2 does not change π1 (Proposition 1.26(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is obtained from X by attaching n-cells with n > 2, the inclusion X ↪ Y induces an isomorphism on π1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: the attaching neighborhoods deformation retract onto spheres S^{n−1} with trivial π1 for n>2, so they do not introduce new relations in π1. Use this to reduce fundamental group computations to the 2-skeleton.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of 2-skeleton induces π1 isomorphism (Proposition 1.26(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a path-connected CW complex X, the inclusion of the 2-skeleton X^2 ↪ X induces an isomorphism π1(X^2,x0) ≈ π1(X,x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequent to (b) and induction for finite-dimensional complexes; for infinite-dimensional complexes use compactness of loop images to find finite skeleta containing the loop and homotopy. Practically, π1 is determined by cells up to dimension 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of surface groups via one 2-cell relator
rubrics_metrics.description: The orientable surface M_g of genus g has a cell structure with one 0-cell, 2g 1-cells, and one 2-cell attached along the word [a1,b1]···[ag,bg]. Hence π1(M_g) ≈ ⟨a1,b1,…,ag,bg | [a1,b1]···[ag,bg]⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 1.26 to get the presentation: start from wedge of 2g circles (free group on 2g generators) and quotient by the normal subgroup generated by the attaching loop word. Abelianization gives Z^{2g}, which is an invariant used to distinguish genus. Nonorientable surfaces are handled similarly (relator a1^2···ag^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wirtinger presentation algorithm for knot complements
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithm: place knot K almost flat so it intersects the table in arcs α_i and crosses β_ℓ; build a 2D complex X deformation retracting R^3 − K by placing strips R_i above α_i and squares S_ℓ over crossing arcs; then π1(R^3 − K) has a generator x_i for each strip R_i and a relation x_i x_j x_i^{-1} = x_k for each square (crossing) as in the figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields the classical Wirtinger presentation. Practical notes: indices and signs depend on orientations of K and the crossing; the abelianization of π1(R^3 − K) obtained from this presentation is Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and local condition for covering spaces (sheets and evenly covered neighborhoods)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covering space p: X f → X satisfies: each x ∈ X has an open neighborhood U such that p^{-1}(U) is a union of disjoint open sets in X each mapped homeomorphically onto U by p. Those U are called evenly covered; the disjoint open sets in p^{-1}(U) are sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets over a connected U are the connected components of p^{-1}(U) and their number equals |p^{-1}(x)| for x ∈ U. The number of sheets is locally constant and hence constant on connected X. Examples: n-fold map S^1 → S^1, p(z)=z^n; infinite-sheeted helix covering R^2−{0}. Disconnected coverings decompose as disjoint unions of connected coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification theorem for connected covering spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a one-to-one correspondence between connected covering spaces of X (up to isomorphism) and conjugacy classes of subgroups of π1(X,x0). If basepoints are kept track of, this is a correspondence between connected basepointed covering spaces and actual subgroups of π1(X,x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In graph examples (covers of S^1 ∨ S^1) covering graphs are given 2-orientations; the universal cover corresponds to the trivial subgroup. Changing basepoint in the cover conjugates the subgroup. Maximal symmetry (vertex-transitive covers) corresponds exactly to normal subgroups, and deck transformation group ≅ π1(X)/N for normal N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifting properties and consequences (homotopy/path lifting, injectivity of p_*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covering maps have the homotopy lifting property: given p:X→X and a map f_0:Y→X with a chosen lift, any homotopy of f_0 lifts uniquely to a homotopy of the lift. Special cases: path lifting and unique lifts of paths. Consequence: the induced map p_*:π1(X, x_0)→π1(X,x0) is injective, and its image consists precisely of homotopy classes of loops at x0 whose lifts starting at x_0 are loops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use uniqueness of lifts to show kernel trivial: a loop in X whose projection is nullhomotopic lifts to a nullhomotopy and thus must have been nullhomotopic already. Conversely, any loop in X that has a loop lift represents an element of the image of p_*. These lifting criteria are basic tools for analyzing subgroups coming from covers.
